notes: Approval date from AstraZeneca's 6-K press release and Drugs@FDA (BLA 761070 original approval 2017-11-14; https://api.fda.gov/drug/drugsfda.json?search=application_number:BLA761070). mechanism: Type I interferon receptor (IFNAR1) antagonist monoclonal antibody
dosing: 300 mg intravenous infusion every 4 weeks; subcutaneous option 120 mg once weekly (from 2026)
first_us_indication: Adult patients with moderate to severe systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) who are receiving standard therapy
notes: FDA approval letter for BLA 761123 signed 07/30/2021. AstraZeneca announced the approval on 2 Aug 2021 (6-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/901832/000165495421008378/a2087h.htm). No further US indications: the current label (openFDA, effective 2026-09-25) still lists adult moderate to severe SLE only. A subcutaneous formulation (prefilled syringe and autoinjector, BLA 761451) was approved 2026-04-24 for the same indication (Drugs@FDA). First US sales $1m in Q3 2021. No UC or CD approval. Note the indication is 'moderate to severe SLE' (FDA letter wording).

notes: FDA approval letter for BLA 761224 (sponsor AstraZeneca AB) signed 12/17/2021; AstraZeneca announced it on 20 Dec 2021 (6-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/901832/000165495421013320/a1228w.htm). SPLIT REPORTING: under the AstraZeneca-Amgen collaboration, Amgen records Tezspire product sales in the US and AstraZeneca records ex-US product sales; AstraZeneca books its share of US gross profit as Collaboration (later Alliance) Revenue (AZ H1 2022 and FY 2022 results). Amgen's first Tezspire sales were $7m in Q1 2022 (no line in Amgen's Q4 2021 release). AZ's first ex-US product sales were $4m in Q4 2022. Each company's figure is kept separately in the sales file (reporting_company); do not add AZ 'World' to Amgen 'World' without care, and never add AZ collaboration revenue. No UC or CD approval.
